financing.summary: Meritage is an investment-grade (BBB-/Baa3/BBB-), balance-sheet land owner: at September 30, 2026 it controlled 71,765 lots, 69% owned and 31% optioned, a 5.3-year supply, and it funds land from operating cash, $1.825 billion of unsecured notes and an undrawn $980 million revolver (cash $677 million, about $1.6 billion of total capacity). The mix has moved the wrong way for a land banker since 2024: owned share rose from 62% at year-end 2024 to 72% at year-end 2025 after the company walked from about 7,200 optioned lots in 2025, and the FY2025 10-K says its participation in land options is limited at this time. No land banker is named in any filing, but in Q1 2026 a new specific-performance structure appeared (consolidated real estate not owned, $126.7 million and 3,960 lots by Q3 2026, with $59.9 million booked as financing proceeds), which reads like a first land-bank-style financing with an undisclosed counterparty. With land spend cut about 40% year over year, $100 million a quarter of buybacks planned and $300 million of 5.125% notes due June 2027 (callable at par from December 6, 2026), there is real room for off-balance-sheet lot capital on roughly 49,000 owned lots, but management has not publicly set an option target.
financing.land_strategy: Owns most. The FY2025 10-K states a goal of a four-to-five-year lot supply, says the company is buying mainly undeveloped or partially developed land and developing it itself because finished lots are scarce, and says its participation in land options is limited at this time. Option contracts typically carry non-refundable deposits of 5% to 20% of purchase price, and land purchases are financed through working capital including corporate borrowings. No owned/optioned target is stated in the FY2025 10-K or the 2026 10-Qs. Mix by quarter from the company's analyst decks: 62% owned / 38% optioned at 12/31/2024 (85,613 lots), 72% / 28% at 12/31/2025 (77,625), 70% / 30% at 3/31/2026 (75,481), 69% / 31% at 6/30/2026 (73,233) and 9/30/2026 (71,765).

lots.source_title: 3Q26 Analyst Call slides, slide 9 (Land & Development Investment); Q3 2026 Form 10-Q Note 3
lots.note: Total (71,765), 69% owned / 31% optioned and 5.3 years supply are stated on the slide. The owned and optioned counts are derived, not stated: the Q3 2026 10-Q Note 3 gives 18,619 lots under committed purchase and option contracts plus 3,960 lots under specific-performance purchase contracts (22,579, which is 31% of 71,765), leaving 49,186 owned. A further 18,025 uncommitted lots under refundable contracts are not counted in the controlled total. At 12/31/2025 the 10-K states the split outright: 55,861 owned plus 21,764 committed option/purchase lots = 77,625.

land_banking.description: From Q1 2026 Meritage reports purchase contracts with a specific performance obligation, recorded on balance sheet as consolidated real estate not owned with a matching liability. It booked $59.9 million of proceeds from these liabilities as a financing cash inflow in Q1 2026. At 9/30/2026: 3,960 lots, $126.7 million of real estate not owned and $115.2 million of related liabilities. The filings do not call this land banking and name no counterparty.
land_banking.source_title: Form 10-Q for the quarter ended September 30, 2026 (filed 2026-10-30), Notes 1 to 3 and financing cash flows
land_banking.note: None existed at 12/31/2025 (FY2025 10-K shows zero). Build-up: 3,161 lots / $65.2 million at 3/31/2026; $70.3 million liability at 6/30/2026; 3,960 lots / $126.7 million at 9/30/2026. Reading it as a land-bank-style financing is this researcher's interpretation of the accounting, not a company statement.

land_banking.counterparty: Not disclosed (various land sellers and development entities)
land_banking.description: Off-balance-sheet purchase and option contracts at 9/30/2026: 36,644 lots with a total purchase price of $2.83 billion secured by $170.8 million of cash deposits. Of these, 18,619 lots ($1.62 billion, $131.8 million of deposits) are committed and 18,025 lots ($1.21 billion, $39.0 million of deposits) are uncommitted and still in evaluation. None requires Meritage to buy; exposure is limited to deposits and capitalised pre-acquisition costs.
land_banking.source_title: Form 10-Q for the quarter ended September 30, 2026 (filed 2026-10-30), Note 3 (lots under option table)
land_banking.note: The 10-Q says lots are acquired from various development entities under purchase and option agreements; no counterparty, land banker or program size is named. At 12/31/2025 the equivalent table showed 36,329 lots, $2.12 billion purchase price, $174.2 million deposits, of which option contracts with non-refundable deposits were 9,559 lots / $947.6 million.

debt.note: principal_usd_m is the commitment, not a drawn balance. No borrowings at 9/30/2026 or during the first nine months of 2026; $83.3 million of letters of credit outstanding, $896.7 million available. Matures June 24, 2031. Accordion to $1.470 billion per the 8-K (the 10-Q rounds to $1.5 billion). Availability is subject to a borrowing base. Covenants at 9/30/2026: minimum tangible net worth $3.61 billion required vs $5.0 billion actual; leverage ratio maximum 60% vs 17.1% actual (Q3 2026 10-Q: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/833079/000083307926000135/mth-20260930.htm). The agent role moved from JPMorgan Chase to Mizuho with this amendment.

gaps: Key-metrics definitions: total debt = senior and convertible senior notes, net ($1,809.4M) plus loans payable and other borrowings ($42.4M) and excludes the $115.2M liability for consolidated real estate not owned; liquidity = cash $677.5M + $896.7M revolver availability (the 10-Q says about $1.6 billion); debt-to-capital 26.9%; stockholders' equity $5,044M. Ratings are from the FY2025 10-K.

Land-banking counterparties: none named in the FY2024 or FY2025 10-K or the Q1 to Q3 2026 10-Qs (text checked for Millrose, Kennedy Lewis, Angelo Gordon, Domain, DW Partners, Essential Housing, IHP Capital, Brookfield, Varde, Oaktree, GTIS, Hearthstone, Walton, Forestar and 'land bank': zero hits). Press and trade press were not searched for these names, so a publicly reported relationship cannot be ruled out.
Counterparty to the specific-performance land purchase contracts first reported in Q1 2026 ($126.7M, 3,960 lots at 9/30/2026): not publicly disclosed.

Earnings-call transcripts (Q4 2025 to Q3 2026) were not read: no transcript is posted on the investor site. Management commentary on off-balance-sheet land financing, any owned/optioned target and plans for the June 2027 notes should be checked there.

Owned and optioned lot counts at 9/30/2026 are derived from stated percentages and the 10-Q option table; the company states only the total and the 69% / 31% split. Lots by region or state are not disclosed.
Land joint-venture partners, locations and JV-level debt: not publicly disclosed.
Lenders on the $42.4M of secured real estate notes payable and their maturities at 9/30/2026: not publicly disclosed.
Rating actions in 2025 and 2026: none identified in company filings; agency releases were not checked (web search unavailable). Ratings shown are as of 12/31/2025.

M&A: no acquisition, merger or divestiture in 2025 or 2026 appears in the FY2025 10-K, the 2026 10-Qs, the 8-K list or the investor-site press releases through 2026-11-19 (goodwill unchanged at $33.0M). Rumoured or third-party-reported deals were not searched (web search unavailable). Context only, outside the window: on October 30, 2024 Meritage announced the purchase of the assets of Elliott Homes (Gulf Coast: Mississippi, Alabama, Florida panhandle; over 5,500 lots), its first acquisition since 2014 (https://investors.meritagehomes.com/news-events-presentations/press-releases/detail/403/meritage-homes-announces-entry-into-the-gulf-coast-markets).

Q1 2026 10-Q shows a committed purchase price of $3.74 billion for 19,740 lots, out of line with $1.33 billion at 12/31/2025 and $1.62 billion at 9/30/2026; not explained in the filing and not relied on here.
